title: The quiet cultural cost of speaking and listening less
teaser: A shrinking habit of listening may be one of the quieter costs of AI. I spent much of my career studying how people speak and tell stories, including leading the National Library of Australia team responsible for the Southern Hemisphere’s largest oral history collection from 2018 to early 2024. Built since 1957, the archive now holds more than 58,000 hours of recordings. Listening again to hundreds of those hours for a book and podcast brought one loss into focus: when we hear less from people unlike ourselves, we have fewer chances to practise empathy.
